hub.speaker: Olesm
hub.text: Oh — hello. One moment; I'm three columns into a supply tally and if I lose the thread I start again from the granary. Sixty-one, sixty-two. There. Olesm, council clerk. How can I help?

text_variants.text: Still counting, this late. The tally has to balance before I sleep, and it doesn't yet.
Oh — hello. You have the look of someone who counts the exits on the way into a room. A [Tactician]? Truly? I so rarely get to talk shop. Sit, sit. Well. Stand. How can I help?
Still up here? The gallery won't map itself, and I'd rather you were down there with a plan than up here with second thoughts. You have the map. Go.
You climbed back out. I confess I ran the odds while you were down there and did not care for them. Tell me it's over. I have a column that badly wants a number in it.

The gallery's sealed and the report is filed, which means my column finally has its number. I would still rather have no construct under my streets at all, but 'under control' is a phrase I can file. My thanks, again.

options.text: [Appraise Foe] What's the city's real weak point?
Zevara sent me. The tunnels under the cisterns. What do you have?
It's dead. Zevara's sealing the gallery.
I'll leave you to your tally.
You run half this city from that desk. You know that, right?
Your uncle's board notice — the gallery he means?
That Watch notice — the gallery survey. I'll take it.
The gallery. It's done — and it's stranger than anyone thought.

options._comment: Act V beat 3, THE TALK PATH (#270), paying off his own shipped seal_kept_report line. Gated on the ward fact alone -- by which route the player learned it is not Olesm's business -- and hidden once the seal is settled by any path. Appended LAST: the gate counter is Act V's own, so no shipped fixture sees this row.
options.text: There's a ward under the city that has to go on being fed. The Watch needs to pay for it.

seal_bounty_pitch._comment: The witch pattern: a Skill leg (visible-LOCKED) and a priced alternate (grey-visible when broke), both landing on the same posted outcome, plus an always-available exit. The Skill does not skip the negotiation -- it IS the negotiation, and it lands on the quest's last beat, not past it. REWARD ADJUDICATION: the posting is FICTION, not a bounties.json row -- a real row would mint accepted_/completed_bounty counters outside this wave's frozen list and re-pin every board canonical; the mechanical payoff is the quest's own resolution_paths grant.
seal_bounty_pitch.speaker: Olesm
seal_bounty_pitch.text: Fed, on a schedule, with no end written anywhere. A posting like that sits on the ledger forever. Every quarter, somebody new asks why we're paying a Gnoll to walk down and feed a door, and every quarter somebody has to be brave enough to sign it again.

options.text: [Charming Smile] You've been dreading that door since the survey. Sign it and sleep.
Then I'll fund the first season myself, and you can explain the second. (12 gold)
I'll come back when I've thought it through.

seal_bounty_posted.speaker: Olesm
seal_bounty_posted.text: Right. Right. Standing notice, Guild board, renewed by the season: one keeper, one lantern of mana a month, no questions logged about what it feeds. I'm putting my name on it, which means when it lapses it will be my fault. That sits better than not knowing did. Thank you.

options.text: Somebody has to hold the door.

seal_bounty_posted._comment: A seal_opened arm, because the FIGHT fork's no-dead-end hatch lets a player who broke the seal and could not finish the warden still fund the keeper. hide_when is FORBIDDEN here -- hiding the arm would close the hatch.

text_variants.text: Right. Right. Standing notice, Guild board, renewed by the season: one keeper, one lantern of mana a month, and a door that is already open at the bottom of it. I'm putting my name on that too. The keeper's first duty changes from feeding it to watching it, and I want that in writing before anyone asks me why. Thank you.

olesm_chess_invite.speaker: Olesm
olesm_chess_invite.text: The board's been out since Tuesday, if you want the honest count. I'm not going to pretend otherwise. Whenever you're ready. You'll have white — let me clear the tally sheets off your side of the desk.

olesm_chess_setup.speaker: Olesm
olesm_chess_setup.text: Not a fresh game, actually. Same position, move for move: my opening, her replies, right up to the moment I stopped seeing straight. Eleven moves in, my bishop's aimed at your king and I am, in my own defense, feeling rather clever about it. Somewhere in here she found a door I didn't. Find it again and I'll believe two people can see the same board the same way.

olesm_chess_puzzle.speaker: Olesm
olesm_chess_puzzle.text: Here. Your rook's pinned to the corner, my bishop threatens mate in three if you sit still, and I am rather pleased with myself. Two gold on it, friendly, either way. What's the move?

options.text: Trade the rook. Knight takes, clear the corner.
Queen takes the bishop. End the threat now.
Ignore the bishop. Push the pawn, threaten mate in two instead.
Play it safe. Offer the draw.

olesm_chess_wrong_pieces.speaker: Olesm
olesm_chess_wrong_pieces.text: Safe. Sound. Exactly what I played that day, and exactly why I lost: I traded fear for fear and never once asked what she wanted. Her plan. I never once looked at her plan. Try again.

olesm_chess_wrong_queen.speaker: Olesm
olesm_chess_wrong_queen.text: The obvious answer. Take the piece and the threat dies with it. I made that exact trade against her, three games earlier, and it taught me nothing. Try again.

olesm_chess_win.speaker: Olesm
olesm_chess_win.text: Oh. Oh no. You'd let the mate stand and walk past it. That's her move. That is exactly her move. I stared at this position for a season and you found the door in one sitting. Here — two gold. I need to write this down before it stops making sense.

olesm_chess_loss.speaker: Olesm
olesm_chess_loss.text: Draw accepted, and the coin with it. My position was lost — I sat with it a season, I know what you had on that board. She played on from here and took me apart. I'm entering it in the book as a draw, two gold to me, and copying the final position in beneath it.

olesm_doubt.speaker: Olesm
olesm_doubt.text: Ha. Ha. No. I run the paperwork the Council ignores, and I'm a [Tactician] whose largest engagement to date was a supply-cart dispute. Which I won. Decisively. I keep a list of what I'd do if Liscor were ever truly tested. It's a good list. It lives in the bottom drawer, and I hope it stays there.

options.text: I hope the list stays theoretical.
The cart never stood a chance.

olesm_doubt_two.speaker: Olesm
olesm_doubt_two.text: So do I. You train your whole life for a day you pray never comes. Meanwhile the list stays in the drawer and I check the granary sums instead. Liscor's had ten quiet years. I like to think a few of them are partly mine.

olesm_ambition.speaker: Olesm
olesm_ambition.text: Honestly? There's a class above mine. [Strategist]. Cities write to theirs. Armies wait on them. Some nights I can almost see the shape of the level, like a move you know is on the board and cannot find yet. I've started writing to other [Tacticians]. Comparing games. Doctrine, where anyone will admit to having one. Mistakes — mine, mostly, in generous detail. It may come to nothing. Or every city ends up wanting a copy of it.

olesm_ambition_two.speaker: Olesm
olesm_ambition_two.text: You'd be the second subscriber. The first is me, checking for errors. Thank you. People ask what I do; you asked what I'm for. I'm leaving the second chair out.

briefing.speaker: Olesm
briefing.text: I mapped your ledge sketches against the city plans. There's a gallery below the cisterns older than Liscor's walls, and something has been widening it. Kill it, chase it off — or map it, a map would serve. The one fixed term: it does not follow you up. Take Relc. Please.

resolution.speaker: Olesm
resolution.text: A Raskghar, awake, under my streets. I get to write that sentence into the minutes now, and initial it. I'm filing this under 'problems the Council pays adventurers for' — which, as of today, includes you. The seal will hold. Probably. Play chess with me sometime; you've earned the good board.

chess.speaker: Olesm
chess.text: Both sides, yes. It's the only honest way to learn how the enemy thinks. You have to want to win as them. A human beat me across this very board once, so thoroughly I nearly thanked her. I did thank her. Best thing to happen to my game in years.

chess_two.speaker: Olesm
chess_two.text: I learned more from that one loss than from ten wins before it. I have the ten wins; I checked. Her game is written out in my desk, second drawer, and I take it out when a Council report has me stuck. It's out on the desk now, as it happens. The granary tally has had me stuck since yesterday.

resonance.speaker: Olesm
resonance.text: The gap in the south wall? The masons watch that; it's on every list the Council owns. The one I lose sleep over is supply. Liscor has never been besieged long enough to learn its own granaries, and my arithmetic gives out in the third hungry week. You already knew that. I can see you did. It is, honestly, a relief not to be the only one in the room doing that arithmetic.

resonance_two.speaker: Olesm
resonance_two.text: I would like that. Genuinely. Bring a board. One afternoon, the wall first, then the war — I'll have the supply figures out before you're through the door.

cisterns.speaker: Olesm
cisterns.text: Worried is the professional term, yes. The market's had reports: things moving under the grates, a cistern gone foul, a fishmonger who swears something looked back at him from the dark. Probably nothing. But it is under a walled city, and I would like to be certain. Actually — you're standing here and you're armed. Would you go down and settle it?

text_variants.text: You're back. The cisterns. Any word? The grate's open now, and I still have no count for what's nesting down there.
There's dust on you from somewhere below street level. The nest under the market. Is it settled? Tell me straight.
Word from the gate says the Watch moved on the cisterns. Was that your doing? I want to hear how it fell out.
You came back with your skin and, unless I misread you, with a picture in your head. You mapped it, didn't you. Show me.
The cisterns are off my ledger and onto the Council's, thanks to you. Quiet streets. I could get used to it.

options.text: I'll look into it. Where do I start?
It's dealt with. I cleared the nest myself.
The Watch swept it. Captain Zevara's people handled it.
I didn't fight it. I mapped it: the nest, the count, the exits. [Appraise Foe]
Let me know if it turns into a something.

cisterns_brief.speaker: Olesm
cisterns_brief.text: Thank you. Here's what I have. Something's nested in the old cisterns under the market — the reports say spiders, big ones, silver-backed, the kind that climb up from the Dungeon when a wall cracks. You get down there by the green sewer-grate off the south square. It's rusted, but it'll open now that someone official wants it open. As for settling it, I genuinely don't mind how. Put a blade through it, or get the Watch to sweep it. Or just bring me a proper picture of what's down there — count, size, exits. I can plan from a page like that, and it costs less in bandages than fighting does. Settle it however suits you, then come tell me it's done.

cisterns_done.speaker: Olesm
cisterns_done.text: Then it's over, and the city's quieter for it. Nobody thanks anyone for this kind of work. So let me do it here: you've the Council's gratitude, and mine, which comes with more paperwork attached. If you ever want a game, or a job that needs a clear head, you know where the board is.

cisterns_intel.speaker: Olesm
cisterns_intel.text: Oh, this is lovely work. You counted them. Exits, chokepoints, the drop where the tunnel falls away. The problem has a shape now, and it fits on one page. The Watch goes in knowing the count and the exits before a boot touches the ladder. This goes into their brief exactly as you drew it. Take the Council's thanks — and mine, doubled, because you did it the clever way.

lism_errand.speaker: Olesm
lism_errand.text: My uncle's notice? That's the same gallery under the cisterns — down the green sewer-grate off the south square, same as I'd send you for the nest. He wants two things confirmed in writing: the old drainage marker, still legible or not, and whether the phosphor moss has spread past the first junction. Both, mind. If one's missing, he'll send the page back and I'll hear about it at dinner.

seal_survey_offer.speaker: Olesm
seal_survey_offer.text: The Watch wants eyes on the reopened gallery — proper eyes. The last guardsman down there filed three words: 'it is dark.' Five gold now, fifteen when you bring me something I can put in a report. The Guild is sending a Silver-rank team to meet you there.

seal_kept_report.speaker: Olesm
seal_kept_report.text: A construct. A vault. Another rune-door — another. Do you know what this does to my casualty projections? Nothing good. Here is your fifteen. Earned.
